recommended_approach: Use Blender Mantaflow liquid simulation configured through the RNA settings classes (notably `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` for the LIQUID domain and `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings` for the inflow/flow object), then bake/cache the simulation and render in Cycles. The doc bundle specifically surfaced Mantaflow-related RNA entry points via `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings` / `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings` attributes (e.g., `flip_ratio`, `noise_strength`, `noise_time_anim`) which indicates the intended programmatic control surface for setting up and tuning a liquid spray + splash + pooling shot.

domain_settings.flip_ratio: (FluidDomainSettings attribute referenced in docs index; use as key tuning control for liquid solver behavior)
domain_settings.noise_strength: (FluidDomainSettings attribute referenced in docs index; available for adding detail/noise where applicable)
domain_settings.noise_time_anim: (FluidDomainSettings attribute referenced in docs index; time animation control for noise where applicable)

flow_settings.flow_type: Inflow/Flow object controlled via bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings (class referenced by docs index)

warnings: Doc bundle results emphasize accessing Blender runtime types via `bpy.types` (Python API overview). If you introduce any custom PropertyGroup helpers in tooling, registration order matters (register lowest-level classes first; unregister in reverse), otherwise Blender raises registration errors (see Python API overview on class registration).
